title: Remove the Theme control from the sidebar footer
description: User request on 2026-10-10: "I am annoyed with the Theme button at the bottom. Should it be there?" and, after the lead's recommendation, "OK. Go ahead and remove that from the sidebar". Theme is a set-once preference. It already lives in Settings > Appearance (System, Light, Dark) and in the ⌘K palette, as in ChatGPT, Claude.ai, Notion, Linear and GitHub, so the sidebar footer keeps only Settings.
acceptance_criteria: Given the sidebar, expanded or collapsed to icons, when it renders, then its footer has no Theme control and keeps Settings.
Given Settings > Appearance and the ⌘K theme command, when used, then they still change the theme as before.
Given the codebase, when this lands, then ThemeToggle and anything used only by it are deleted, with their tests. ThemeProvider and the theme context stay.
test_cases: Sidebar: no element named Theme; Settings link present.
Settings Appearance and palette theme command still switch the theme.
verification: Red first: src/components/shell/shell.test.tsx, before AppSidebar.tsx changed: 2 failed | 17 passed (19); both new sidebar tests failed on the Theme span (expanded and collapsed). Green: npx vitest run src/components/shell src/components/theme src/features/settings: Test Files 9 passed (9), Tests 80 passed (80). App.test.tsx retargeted to Settings > Appearance: 8 passed (8). npm run check (typecheck, eslint, vitest) on the final tree: Test Files 90 passed (90), Tests 722 passed (722), exit 0. An earlier check run failed one test (App.test.tsx theme-menu) because it opened the removed sidebar menu; retargeted to Settings and rerun green. npm run build: exit 0 on the final tree.
